chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
The medicine of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was thyme, and he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'It becomes for the stomach a lining like the lining of the plush brocade.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْقَطِيفَة: Plush brocade or soft velvet fabric

ai.seo_question: What was the medicinal remedy of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and how did he describe its effect on the stomach?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights thyme (*sa'tar*) as a prophylactic for gastric health, using the metaphor of *qatifa*—a fine, soft fabric—to describe how it coats and protects the stomach lining. This reflects the Shia tradition of integrating practical medicine with spiritual wisdom, emphasizing the Sunnah of the Imams in daily health maintenance. The comparison underscores the gentle yet effective nature of thyme in soothing digestive ailments.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ziyad Al Qandy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said:
‘The medicine of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was the thyme, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘It comes to the stomach as velvet like the plush brocade’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ziyad al-Qandiy who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the medicine of ’Amir al-Mu’minin was wild thyme, ’Amir al-Mu’minin would say, Thyme becomes fuzz and fluff for the stomach like that of velvet.’”
